engine: markdown
title: "Arrow IPC"
---

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

Files ending in `.arrow`, `.ipc`, or `.feather` are read with
[arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/). Write Arrow IPC output with
`-O arrow` or by naming the output accordingly.

## Reading

```{term}
rush run -o mtcars.arrow 'df' mtcars.csv
rush run 'head(df, 3) |> dplyr::select(mpg, cyl, hp)' mtcars.arrow
```

## Writing

```{term}
rush run -o subset.arrow 'dplyr::filter(df, mpg > 25)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' subset.arrow
```

## Using `-O arrow` with output flag

```{term}
rush run -O arrow -o sample.arrow 'head(df, 5)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'ncol(df)' sample.arrow
```

## Alternative extensions

The `.feather` and `.ipc` extensions are also recognized:

```{term}
cp mtcars.arrow mtcars.feather
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.feather
cp mtcars.arrow mtcars.ipc
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.ipc
rm -f mtcars.feather mtcars.ipc
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.arrow subset.arrow sample.arrow
```
